concerns.text: Task T016 implements a hard exit (code 1) if success_rate < 0.95. This violates SC-005 which defines success as '≥ 95%' but requires the system to *measure and report* the quality. By crashing, the system prevents the generation of the required success metric report for cases where the rate is 90% (a valid measurement of failure), effectively weakening the requirement to 'must achieve 95% or crash' instead of 'must measure and report if ≥ 95% or < 95%'.

FR-009 mandates that if metadata (temperature, solvent, substrate class) is missing, the *entire dataset* must be excluded immediately. Tasks T011a through T012 implement a granular, row-level processing pipeline that generates intermediate artifacts (e.g., `intermediate_sn1.csv`, `cleaned_intermediate.csv`) even when the fatal 'ABORTED' condition should halt the process. This creates a logical contradiction where the system processes data it is required to exclude entirely, violating the 'all-or-nothing' exclusion constraint.

FR-006 requires a sensitivity analysis sweeping 'top-k descriptors' (input features). Tasks T036 and T029B implement a perturbation study that removes 'top-k atoms' (molecular graph nodes) or aggregates SHAP values at the atom level. This conflates the 'descriptor' entity defined in the spec with the 'atom' entity, failing to verify the robustness of the specific electronic descriptors (Gasteiger/topological) mandated by FR-006.

FR-007 requires a collinearity diagnostic (VIF) on 'distinct descriptor classes' and explicitly excludes Gasteiger charges. Task T028 only references the input CSV without explicitly defining the logic to group features by class or implement the exclusion of Gasteiger charges. This risks calculating VIF on a mixed feature set, violating the specific constraint of FR-007.

T040 requires 'dynamic budgeting' to reduce hyperparameter search configurations if N ≥ 2000 to meet SC-002 (6-hour limit). The task description relies on `main.py` execution without a specific task to implement the `--max-configs` argument logic or the timeout mechanism in `code/models/train.py` itself. This leaves the 'dynamic' aspect of the plan unimplemented in the task list, risking a violation of the 6-hour constraint.
